title: QuIC Welcomes the European Quantum Act, Pledges to 'Mobilize Industry'
html:
Insider Brief

  • The European Quantum Industry Consortium (QuIC) welcomed the European Commission’s proposed Quantum Act and called for stronger measures to help European quantum companies scale.
  • QuIC plans to ask lawmakers for €7.7 billion to €12.3 billion in public procurement commitments over five years and a dedicated quantum share of the proposed Sovereign Tech Equity Fund.
  • QuIC will consult its more than 240 member organizations over two weeks to develop recommendations for the European Parliament and Council.

PRESS RELEASE — The European Quantum Industry Consortium (QuIC) welcomes the publication of the European Commission’s proposal for the European Quantum Act, marking a significant milestone in Europe’s ambition to establish itself as a global leader in quantum technologies.

As Europe’s largest quantum industry consortium, QuIC is committed to supporting the ambitions of the Quantum Act and ensuring that the expertise, priorities and needs of the European quantum industry are represented throughout the legislative process.

The Quantum Act presents an important opportunity to strengthen Europe’s industrial competitiveness, accelerate the commercialisation and adoption of quantum technologies, and establish the conditions necessary for a sustainable, resilient and globally competitive quantum ecosystem.

QuIC‘s initial assessment of the European Quantum Act

QuIC welcomes a proposal that sets common European priorities for quantum, from research to public procurement, and takes up several asks the industry has made since 2025:

  • Public procurement as a tool of industrial policy. Public buyers must set requirements on security of supply, interoperability and lifecycle support. Contracts are reserved for Union-controlled suppliers, with defined routes for partner countries that offer reciprocity. Suppliers that perform substantial development, manufacturing or processing qualify, which includes European system integrators.
  • The Sovereign Tech Equity Fund. The Act allows the Union to set up an equity vehicle with Member States and other investors, which will help fund the Quantum Europe Framework Initiative.
  • Grand challenges. They are technology-neutral and run on milestones, measured in logical qubits rather than physical qubit counts.
  • Post-quantum cryptography. Public administrations must buy post-quantumready and crypto-agile products for their critical systems, from six months after entry into force, a first step towards quantum-safe communication.
  • Supply-chain resilience. Critical quantum components and dependencies will be monitored at European level.

To turn these priorities into industrial scale, QuIC will ask Parliament and Council to add:

  • Procurement volumes. €300–500 million of commitments within six months of entry into force, and €7.7–12.3 billion over five years, across all national and European public buyers.
  • A quantum share in the Sovereign Tech Equity Fund. The share should be open to scale-ups as well as start-ups, with a start date and decision times that match the pace of competition with the United States and China.
  • A route to industrial production. Quantum foundries need a path from pilot lines to industrial production, across the Quantum Act and the Chips Act 2.0.
  • Fast-track procedures for strategic quantum projects, as in the Chips Act 2.0.
  • A defined role for industry where priorities are set.

“The European Quantum Act represents a defining opportunity for Europe to translate its scientific and technological excellence into industrial leadership. It is essential that the expertise, ambitions and needs of our industry are reflected in this legislative

framework. Together, we can help shape a competitive, resilient and globally recognised European quantum ecosystem.” Dr. Thomas Strohm, President of QuIC

Mobilising the European quantum industry

To ensure a coordinated and representative industry response, QuIC is launching a dedicated two-week sprint, with planning commencing on Friday, 27 November 2026.

Led by QuIC‘s Executive Director and leadership team, the initiative will bring together expertise from across its community of more than 240 member organisations, spanning start-ups, SMEs, large industrial corporations, research organisations, investors and other stakeholders across the quantum value chain.

The consultation will gather industry perspectives on:

  • The strategic priorities and proposed measures outlined in the Quantum Act.
  • Opportunities to accelerate industrial growth, investment and commercialisation.
  • Potential regulatory, financial and operational barriers.
  • European competitiveness, technological sovereignty and supply chain resilience.
  • The new restrictions on subcontractors and critical components in public procurement.
  • The scope of the post-quantum procurement obligation.
  • Quantum technology adoption and market development.
  • Recommendations for strengthening the proposed legislative framework.

The findings will form the basis of a consolidated QuIC position paper, providing the

European Parliament and the Council with actionable, industry-driven recommendations

Ensuring every industry voice is heard

QuIC recognises that the success of the European Quantum Act will depend on its ability to address the diverse needs of the European quantum ecosystem.

The consultation will provide all QuIC members and affiliates with an opportunity to contribute their expertise, regardless of their organisation’s size, maturity or technological focus.

“Our responsibility is to give the European quantum industry a strong and representative voice in shaping the Quantum Act. The Act sets the right priorities, and for the industry to scale it now needs public procurement volumes and growth capital. We start from a first draft built with our members’ feedback, and every member can contribute to it from Friday.” Dr. Cécile Perrault, Executive Director of QuIC

A collaborative approach to Europe’s quantum future

QuIC looks forward to continued constructive engagement with the European Commission, European institutions, policymakers and industry stakeholders throughout the legislative process.

Through its established network, technical expertise and industry-led policy activities, QuIC remains committed to supporting the development of a legislative framework that enables European quantum businesses to innovate, scale and compete globally.

Organisations interested in contributing to QuIC‘s industry-led policy initiatives and becoming part of Europe’s largest quantum industry consortium are invited to explore membership opportunities at www.euroquic.org or contact [email protected].

Matt Swayne
